principles: Serialize scarce workspace validation capacity at the official command boundary while preserving story-scoped evidence isolation.
Make contention observable and self-resolving: wait asynchronously, report the live holder, then run automatically.
Use one canonical git-common-dir lock and one fixed global-to-story acquisition order.
Keep proof budgets and command inventories unchanged; coordination must remove contention rather than weaken gates.
Fail closed on deadline, abort, malformed ownership, or unrecoverable lock state.
drivers: Different-story and no-story official validations currently bypass one another because the existing lock key contains storyId.
Synchronous polling would block Node timers and can stale the active heartbeat in same-process or nested execution.
DONE-required and routine validation must retain distinct evidence artifacts, freshness rules, and configured timeout budgets.

options.name: A: Replace the story lock with one global fail-fast lock
cons: Conflates capacity coordination with story evidence ownership

options.name: B: Re-key the current story lock globally and use synchronous lock polling
cons: Can block heartbeat and abort timers
Makes reentrancy and diagnostics harder to reason about

options.name: C: Add an outer asynchronous workspace capacity lease and retain the inner story evidence lock
pros: Covers story and no-story official validate entrypoints
Preserves current evidence isolation and stale classification
Supports bounded progress, cooperative abort, and automatic continuation
Keeps a mechanically enforceable global-to-story order
cons: Requires a small asynchronous acquisition loop

options.name: D: Also coordinate direct npm test through inherited environment tokens
cons: Expands scope into arbitrary child-process and user-shell coordination
Risks deadlock when official validation itself invokes npm test
Violates the explicit bare npm test exclusion

chosen: C: Add an outer asynchronous workspace capacity lease and retain the inner story evidence lock
rationale: Option C fixes the actual capacity race at the two official product entrypoints, including validate without a story ID, while retaining the existing per-story evidence lock as an inner defense. Async acquisition keeps heartbeat and cancellation live, and the fixed global-to-story order avoids lock inversion without changing any proof budget.

preMortem.scenario: The waiter blocks the event loop while polling.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation calls synchronous acquireMkdirLock waiting mode or Atomics.wait.
preMortem.consequence: Holder heartbeat or timeout watchdog stops refreshing and a live lease is misclassified stale.
preMortem.mitigation: Attempt short fail-fast acquisitions and delay with an awaited timer; add a smoke proving heartbeat advances while a second caller waits.

preMortem.scenario: A no-story lattice validate still competes with a story validation.
preMortem.trigger: Capacity wrapping is added only inside existing story-aware branches.
preMortem.consequence: The exact observed contention remains possible and canonical tests still time out.
preMortem.mitigation: Wrap the entire official validate execution regardless of story ID; keep only the inner evidence lock conditional on story ID.

preMortem.scenario: Nested validation deadlocks on its own capacity lease.
preMortem.trigger: The outer lease does not inherit AsyncLocalStorage ownership.
preMortem.consequence: An official handler invoking a nested protected operation waits forever on itself.
preMortem.mitigation: Track capacity and story lock keys in the existing async owner context and prove same-context reentrancy.

preMortem.scenario: Queue time silently weakens or expands timeout guarantees.
preMortem.trigger: The fix rewrites command timeout or deadline budgets to accommodate waiting.
preMortem.consequence: PASS evidence no longer represents the documented 120, 180, or 300 second gates.
preMortem.mitigation: Leave configured commands and budgets byte-for-byte unchanged; deadline/abort may stop waiting before callback entry.

preMortem.scenario: A crash leaves every validation permanently queued.
preMortem.trigger: Capacity heartbeat stops and stale ownership is never reclaimed.
preMortem.consequence: Official validation cannot run without manual filesystem surgery.
preMortem.mitigation: Reuse pid, process-start, heartbeat, ownership-checked release, and stale classifier behavior; add dead-holder reclaim and throw-release proofs.

preMortem.scenario: Bare npm test is incorrectly assumed to participate.
preMortem.trigger: Help text does not disclose the coordination boundary.
preMortem.consequence: Users run direct npm test beside official validation and recreate resource contention.
preMortem.mitigation: State in CLI help or diagnostics that only lattice validate and lattice done_required_validate acquire the lease and bare npm test must not run concurrently.
